bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Coking coal price volatility; INR depreciation impacting FX costs; global steel demand slowdown; China export surplus suppressing prices; capex execution delays (e.g., Utkal, Dolvi); regulatory delays in mining; labor cost inflation; geopolitical risks in overseas operations; transition risks in green steel tech deployment
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and forward-looking; emphasized operational excellence, deleveraging via JV, and green steel leadership; highlighted digitalisation (Vision.AI) as key to cost and safety gains; expressed strong conviction in India’s steel demand growth and export resilience; tone was upbeat on FY26 guidance and FY31 capacity targets
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: JSW Steel’s BPSL JV effectively transfers ₹37,000cr debt to a 50:50 JV entity, improving balance sheet without equity dilution; JSW One’s ₹1,306cr credit GMV indicates successful financial services monetisation beyond steel; 30% stake in Illawarra coal mine secures long-term coking coal supply; digital AI platform (Vision.AI) projected to save ₹100cr/year across plants; 61% VASP sales mix is among highest globally for integrated producers
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Net debt to equity improved significantly to 0.42x and net debt to EBITDA to 1.46x, following the JSW JFE JV deleveraging.
- Credit ratings were upgraded by Fitch (BB to BB+, Positive Outlook) and CARE (AA to AA+), reflecting improved financial metrics.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Fully integrated operations from mining through steelmaking to downstream value-added manufacturing, supporting a position among the lowest-cost steel producers globally
- Backward integration with 25 iron ore mines (13 operational) and four coking coal mines, reducing reliance on external raw material procurement
- Strong rail, road and port connectivity lowering logistics costs for raw material sourcing and product delivery
- Leading value-added and special products (VASP) franchise — 61% share of sales mix, with technology access via JFE Steel partnership for high-value special steel products
- Large export footprint to more than 100 countries and one of the country's largest galvanising and coated-steel capacities
- Strategic technology and capital partnerships (JFE Steel, Marubeni-Itochu, Severfield plc) enabling capital-efficient capacity and technology access
- Structurally lower energy cost trajectory via renewable energy commissioning/approvals, waste heat recovery, process gas utilisation and biomass substitution
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Global macro and geopolitical uncertainty — Escalation of conflict in the Middle East disrupted commodity markets, intensified inflationary pressures and weakened global growth expectations during 2026 (global growth projected at 3.1% in 2026 versus 3.4% in 2024 and 2025), a relevant backdrop for a globally exposed, capital-intensive steel producer.
- Tightening global financial conditions and elevated public debt — Volatile energy prices, elevated public debt and tighter long-term financial conditions were flagged as continuing to weigh on the global outlook, particularly for emerging and developing economies, which is relevant to funding costs and capital access for the Company's large capex programme.

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Raw material self-reliance: build captive iron ore and coking coal supply (25 iron ore mines, four coking coal mines, Mozambique and Illawarra coal assets) targeting about 50% captive sourcing of iron ore and coking coal by FY 2030-31 and beyond, to reduce exposure to global price volatility
- Move up the value curve: grow Value-Added and Special Products (VASP) share of sales to reduce earnings cyclicality and improve margin resilience, including new CRGO/electrical steel capacity for India's electrification and EV ambitions
- Capital-efficient capacity growth through strategic partnerships and selective acquisitions (JFE Steel JV for BPSL, POSCO JV for a greenfield Odisha plant, Marubeni-Itochu JV for steel service centres, Severfield plc JV for structural steel) rather than solely organic capex
- Scale India capacity to meet the country's rising steel demand, including Vijayanagar brownfield expansion, Jagatsinghpur and Kadapa greenfield/EAF projects, and the BMM Ispat acquisition
- Decarbonisation as a competitiveness and market-access lever: a two-phase roadmap combining renewable energy integration, green hydrogen, biomass substitution, material circularity and digital optimisation, funded via a dedicated capital allocation shift away from fossil fuels
- Deploy AI-enabled digital solutions and an integrated control tower across manufacturing, supply chain, mining, finance, HR and sales to improve productivity, asset reliability and safety outcomes
- Zero-harm safety culture reinforced through leadership accountability, AI-driven predictive risk identification, immersive training and digital safety platforms
- Grow JSW One, a technology-enabled marketplace (JSW Steel holds 60.79% fully diluted stake), to simplify procurement, financing and logistics for MSME customers
- The Board proposed a final dividend for FY 2025-26, subject to shareholder approval at the 32nd AGM (Friday, 24 July 2026), continuing the Company's practice of annual dividend distribution to equity shareholders. Separately, the Board sought shareholder consent at the same AGM for potential issuance of Non-Convertible Debentures (with warrants convertible/exchangeable into equity shares) and/or equity shares and/or other convertible securities to Qualified Institutional Buyers, indicating a readiness to access capital markets to fund growth alongside continued dividend payouts.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Vijayanagar Blast Furnace-3 capacity upgrade from 3.0 MTPA to 4.5 MTPA was under shutdown since end-September 2025 and was under testing/commissioning at end-March 2026; the 4th and final 3 MTPA battery of Coke Oven #5 was commissioned in Q4 FY 2025-26. Domestic installed crude steel capacity (excluding JVs) is targeted to expand from ~32 MTPA to 50 MTPA by FY 2029-30 and further to 62 MTPA by FY 2031-32, via a balanced mix of brownfield and greenfield expansion plus strategic partnerships, including potential expansion at Utkal, green steel development at Salav, enhanced EAF capacity at Kadapa, and evaluation of growth opportunities at Keonjhar (Odisha) and Gadchiroli (Maharashtra); including JVs, domestic installed capacity is targeted to grow from 36.4 MTPA in FY 2025-26 to 53.3 MTPA by FY 2029-30 and 78 MTPA by FY 2031-32. Growth JVs include expansion at JSW JFE Steel and a proposed 6 MTPA greenfield project with POSCO. Management states brownfield expansions have historically been completed in about 3.5 years at costs below $600/tonne. CRGO electrical-steel capacity is targeted to grow from a current 50,000 TPA to 350,000 TPA by FY 2028-29 via expansion of the Nashik facility (50,000 to 250,000 TPA) and an additional 100,000 TPA line at Vijayanagar, backed by captive hot-rolled coil supply. JSW Steel Coated Products Limited (JSCPL) is augmenting downstream coated-products capacity from 5.2 MTPA to 6.6 MTPA through two new galvanising lines at Khopoli, Maharashtra (CGL#2: 0.36 MTPA galvanised steel with Galvalume provision; CGL#3: 0.5 MTPA Zero-Spangle Galvanised/Zinc-Aluminium-Magnesium products plus a 0.6 MTPA cold rolling mill) and a new galvanising line (0.36 MTPA, with Galvalume provision) plus a new 0.20 MTPA tinplate facility at Rajpura, Punjab. JVML commissioned a 4.5 MTPA capacity Blast Furnace and a 3.3 MTPA Steel Melt Shop (one converter, both casters fully operational in FY 2024-25), with a second SMS converter commissioned in August 2025. BPSL's capacity expansion Phase-1 (2.75 to 3.5 MTPA) was commissioned in Q4 FY 2023 and Phase-2 (3.5 to 4.5 MTPA) in Q2 FY 2025; its 4.5 MTPA integrated plant at Jharsuguda, Odisha was subsequently transferred into the JSW JFE Steel JV on 27 March 2026. Neotrex Steel's LRPC facility at Vijayanagar (144,000 TPA total) was built in two 72,000-TPA phases, commissioned December 2022 and June 2024. Other operational-efficiency commissionings during FY 2025-26 included a MEROS-based waste gas recirculation and bag filter system at Sinter Plant 2 (February 2026), a BF-2 dehumidifier system (October 2025), revamped CDQ 2 and 3 chamber refractory (July 2025), a Phase 2 refractory store adding ~17,000 MT storage capacity (October 2025), and a BFG injection system in the CDQ boiler at Coke Oven 2 (November 2025).
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's infrastructure investment programme (Government capex up more than threefold since FY 2019-20), housing expansion, urbanisation and a manufacturing resurgence are expected to sustain strong domestic steel demand over the medium term
- Domestic steel consumption grew 7.9% in FY 2025-26 to over 164 MnT and is projected to grow 7-9% in FY 2026-27, adding 12-14 million tonnes of incremental demand, though growth is expected to moderate from three successive years of 7%+ growth due to external headwinds
- Imposition of safeguard duties in late December 2025 curbed unfair/predatory steel imports, helping India close FY 2025-26 as a broadly balanced/small net exporter after two years as a net importer, and supported a recovery in domestic steel prices in Q4 FY 2025-26
- Global steel demand outside China is expected to grow amid soft China property-linked demand; China's anti-involution policies and export licensing rules are expected to moderate elevated Chinese exports over time, potentially easing pricing pressure on JSW's realisations
- Rising global trade protectionism (US Section 232 tariff hikes to 50%, EU import quota cuts and CBAM entering its definitive phase in January 2026) creates both a headwind (export market access) and a domestic tailwind (risk of import diversion into India from global overcapacity)
- Automotive sector momentum, aided by GST-rate-driven affordability improvements, and highest-ever sales across auto, renewable energy and appliances segments underpin higher-value product demand
- Structural long runway: India's per-capita steel consumption (~115 kg) remains well below global averages, and the National Steel Policy targets 300 MnT of national crude steel capacity by end of the decade (from an estimated ~220 MnT in FY 2025-26), implying a multi-decade industry growth opportunity
- Shift in sales mix toward Value-Added and Special Products (61% of sales in FY 2025-26, historically up from 25% in FY 2013-14) is cited as reducing earnings cyclicality and improving margin resilience
- Availability of iron ore relative to steel capacity growth is flagged as a key industry constraint, with government auctioning of mines and encouragement of low-grade ore use seen as supportive
- JSW Piombino (Italy) holds two long-term rail supply contracts with Rete Ferroviaria Italiana (RFI), Italy's national rail infrastructure operator, originally worth €359 million, with a Framework Agreement providing milestones to increase contract value to up to approximately €1,277 million

deepdive.thesis: JSW Steel delivered record sales and EBITDA in Q3FY26 driven by 14% YoY volume growth and 61% VASP penetration, while accelerating deleveraging via a ₹37,000cr JV with JFE Steel and scaling green steel capex; the company is on track to reach 50mtpa capacity by FY31 with superior margins and digital-led cost efficiency.

open.item: Fourth coke oven battery (4 x 0.75mtpa) at Vijayanagar to be commissioned by end of FY26.
Expect to spend Rs 15,000-16,000 crore of capex during FY26.
Vijayanagar BF-3 upgradation (adding 1.5mtpa), under planned shutdown since end-Sep 2025, expected to be commissioned by end of Q4 FY26.
50:50 BPSL JV with JFE Steel (equity value Rs 31,500 cr; JFE investing Rs 15,750 cr for 50%) will enable deleveraging of ~Rs 37,000 crore for JSW Steel; transaction expected completed by Q3 FY27.
30mtpa slurry pipeline (302km) and 30mtpa Jatadhar Port for Utkal to be commissioned by FY27.
Dolvi Phase-III expansion from 10 to 15mtpa (long lead items ordered) to be completed by Sep'27.
Two pellet plants (8mtpa each) at Utkal to be commissioned by FY28.
Vijayanagar 0.4mtpa CGL by June 2028 and 0.55mtpa CRNO plant by March 2028; Khopoli 0.6mtpa CRM and 0.86mtpa CGL by Q1 FY28.
Kadapa 1mtpa EAF & section mill and Raigarh 1mtpa structural mill both to be commissioned by FY29; Rajpura Tinplate+CGL by FY28.
Targets 19% reduction in specific energy consumption to 5.65 Gcal/tcs and 39% reduction in specific water consumption to 2.21 m3/tcs by FY30.
Target 42% reduction of CO2 emission intensity to 1.95 tCO2/tcs by FY30 (from 2005 baseline), aligned with India's NDCs.
JSW Utkal Steel integrated plant Phase-I of 5mtpa (capex Rs 31,600 crore) at Jagatsinghpur, Odisha, to be commissioned by FY30.
BPSL JV (JSW Sambalpur) plan to expand to 10mtpa by 2030, from current 4.5mtpa.
Growth path to reach 50mtpa steel capacity in India by FY31 (excluding BPSL), up from ~35.7mt current.
Targeting net neutrality in carbon emissions by 2050.
Target to maintain more than 50% share of Value-Added and Special Products (VASP) in total sales; VASP share at 61% in Q3.
Committed to keep net gearing (ND/Equity) within stated cap of 1.75x and leverage (ND/EBITDA) within stated cap of 3.75x; currently 0.92x and 2.91x.
Energy transition: 2.5GW of RE and 320MWh battery storage capacity approved, of which ~1GW capacity commissioned.
Contemplating introduction of an energy surcharge as a separate line item to pass on unsustainable coking coal price increases to customers.
